mainTopic: Who may perform each stage of the פרה אדומה: רב and שמואל on the כהן, and רבנן and רבי יהודה on gathering, קידוש and sprinkling
overview: This עמוד continues the גמרא's line-by-line reading of the פסוקים of פרה אדומה, asking who may perform each stage. It first finishes an earlier point: the views on "אותה" differ when a donkey is taken out with the פרה. Then רב and שמואל read "לפניו," "אלעזר" and "הכהן" according to their views. רב holds that a כהן is needed throughout, and even a כהן הדיוט is enough. שמואל holds that a זר may slaughter, but אלעזר must take the blood. The repeated word "הכהן" teaches that the כהן must be בכיהונו, even לדורות. The גמרא defends this rule with the idea that the תורה sometimes writes out a קל וחומר. Next it learns that a זר and an אשה may gather the ashes, but a חרש, שוטה and קטן may not. It then brings the dispute between רבנן and רבי יהודה over who may do קידוש and who may dip the hyssop, and each side reads every word of the פסוקים. The עמוד ends with a משנה about sprinkling that seems to contradict רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The practical difference: taking a donkey out with the heifer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion. The difference between the two readings of "אותה" shows up when a donkey is taken out together with the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference is a case where someone took out a donkey with it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the discussion that came on the previous עמוד. It names the exact case where the two views about the word "אותה" give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids taking another animal out with the פרה only because people might mix up which animal was slaughtered. A donkey cannot be mistaken for a cow, so he allows it. רבי reads "אותה" as a strict rule with no reason attached, so even a donkey is excluded.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a discussion that began on the previous עמוד. It answers an earlier question about what the practical difference between the views is. It is not a new topic.

phrases.english: where one took out a donkey with it.
phrases.notes: No one would confuse a donkey with the red cow, so the concern about a mix-up does not apply here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier dispute over "והוציא אותה" by naming the case where it matters.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The views differ when a donkey is taken out together with the פרה.

steps.title: "And he shall slaughter it": no other animal slaughtered with it
steps.stepSummary: The word "אותה" in "ושחט אותה" teaches that no other animal may be slaughtered together with the פרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he shall slaughter it": this teaches that he should not slaughter another animal along with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the פסוק. It reads the word "it" as excluding any other animal at the time of שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as "אותה" in the taking-out stage meant the פרה goes out alone, "אותה" here means it is slaughtered alone. The word "it" is read as a limit: only this animal.

phrases.english: "And he shall slaughter it"
that he should not slaughter another along with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the phrase-by-phrase reading with the next word in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No other animal may be slaughtered together with the פרה אדומה.

steps.title: "Before him": רב and שמואל read it differently
steps.stepSummary: רב reads "לפניו" as "he must not take his mind off it." שמואל reads it as "a זר may slaughter while אלעזר watches."
steps.simpleTranslation: "Before him": according to רב, he should not take his mind off it. According to שמואל, a non-priest slaughters and אלעזר watches.
steps.whatsHappening: Each of the two אמוראים reads "לפניו" in a way that fits his own view about whether a זר may slaughter the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a כהן must slaughter, so for him "before him" cannot mean that someone else slaughters. He reads it as a rule of focus: the כהן must keep his full attention on the פרה. שמואל holds that a זר may slaughter, so he reads "before him" literally: someone else does the שחיטה in front of אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: take his mind off; become distracted

steps.whyThisMatters: This step sets up how each אמורא will explain the next verses. Each later reading follows from how he understood "לפניו" here.

phrases.english: "Before him": according to Rav
that he should not take his mind off it,
according to Shmuel: that a non-priest may slaughter
while Elazar watches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase in the same פסוק; this one splits into two readings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the slaughterer must not be distracted from the פרה. שמואל: a זר may slaughter in front of אלעזר.

steps.title: שמואל: the blood stage goes back to אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: For שמואל, naming "אלעזר" at the blood stage brings the job back to אלעזר after a זר was allowed to slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And אלעזר the כהן shall take some of its blood with his finger": according to שמואל, this returns the task to אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the next פסוק and first gives שמואל's explanation of why אלעזר is named here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the שחיטה could be done by a זר. Without a new instruction, one might think the next stages could also be done by anyone. Mentioning אלעזר again tells us that taking the blood must be done by אלעזר himself.

phrases.english: "And Elazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger"
according to Shmuel: to return it to Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on שמואל's reading of "לפניו" (a זר slaughters).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking the blood must be done by אלעזר himself.

steps.title: רב: a double limitation includes even a כהן הדיוט
steps.stepSummary: For רב, "אלעזר" here is a second limitation after an earlier one. Two limitations in a row widen the law, so even a כהן הדיוט may do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב, this is a limitation after a limitation. A limitation after a limitation only comes to include more, teaching that even an ordinary כהן may do it.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives רב's explanation of why אלעזר is named at the blood stage. For רב, the job never left the כהן, so it needs no "return."
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the earlier mention of אלעזר at the שחיטה already limited the job to a כהן. Naming אלעזר again is a second limitation. By the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, two limitations in a row cancel into an inclusion, so any כהן הדיוט qualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: an ordinary כהן (not כהן גדול or סגן)

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but two limitations in a row do not make the rule stricter. By this rule of דרשה, they widen it.

phrases.english: according to Rav: it is a limitation after a limitation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת,
phrases.english: and a limitation after a limitation comes only to include,
that even an ordinary priest is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's competing explanation of the same word "אלעזר" that שמואל explained in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a כהן הדיוט may perform the פרה service.

steps.title: שמואל: "הכהן" at the cedar stage means even a כהן הדיוט
steps.stepSummary: For שמואל, saying "הכהן" instead of "אלעזר" at the cedar, hyssop and crimson stage shows that a כהן הדיוט is enough here.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the כהן shall take cedar wood, hyssop and crimson wool": according to שמואל, this teaches that even an ordinary כהן may do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a later פסוק and gives שמואל's reading of the word "הכהן" there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the blood stage required אלעזר specifically, the סגן. Here the תורה switches to just "הכהן." That change lowers the requirement to any כהן הדיוט.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן עֵץ אֶרֶז וְאֵזוֹב וּשְׁנִי תוֹלָעַת״,
phrases.english: "And the priest shall take cedar wood, and hyssop, and crimson wool"
according to Shmuel: that even an ordinary priest may do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָקַח הַכֹּהֵן עֵץ אֶרֶז וְאֵזוֹב וּשְׁנִי תוֹלָעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from שמואל's view in step 4 that the blood stage required אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing in the cedar, hyssop and crimson wool may be done by a כהן הדיוט.

steps.title: רב: the word "הכהן" is still needed at the cedar stage
steps.stepSummary: For רב, who already allows a כהן הדיוט, the word "הכהן" is needed for a different reason. Otherwise we might think no כהן is required at all, since these items are not part of the פרה's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב, it is needed. You might have thought that since these items are not the body of the פרה, no כהן is needed. So the תורה teaches us that a כהן is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: for רב, the word "הכהן" seems unnecessary, so why is it there? It explains what wrong idea the word prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, a כהן הדיוט was already allowed from step 5, so "הכהן" cannot be teaching that. Instead it blocks a mistake. Since the cedar, hyssop and crimson are separate items and not the פרה itself, one might think a זר could handle them, so the word teaches that a כהן is still required.

keyTerms.meaning: it would have entered your mind to say
the body of the פרה itself

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a כהן is needed at every stage, and even a כהן הדיוט is fine. שמואל: a זר may slaughter, אלעזר must take the blood, and a כהן הדיוט may do the cedar stage. Each reading of "אלעזר" and "הכהן" follows from the view the אמורא started with.

phrases.english: according to Rav: it was needed,
for it would have entered your mind to say:
since they are not the body of the cow itself,
they should not require a priest,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב's explanation of the same word שמואל explained in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows the word is needed to block a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the cedar, hyssop and crimson are not the פרה's body, a זר could handle them.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כהן is required even for these items.

steps.title: The כהן must be in his priestly state, now and in future generations
steps.stepSummary: The repeated word "הכהן" in the verse teaches that the כהן must be בכיהונו (in his priestly state), and that this rule applies לדורות as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the כהן shall wash his clothes" means the כהן must be in his priestly state. "And the כהן shall be impure until evening" means a כהן in his priestly state is needed in future generations too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא learns two rules from two places where the verse says "הכהן." The first teaches that the כהן must be בכיהונו, and the second teaches that this applies לדורות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse already told us a כהן is involved, so repeating "הכהן" must teach something new. The first repetition adds that he must be בכיהונו, meaning wearing בגדי כהונה and fit for service. The second repetition makes sure this is not only a one-time rule for אלעזר in the מדבר but for every later פרה too.

keyTerms.meaning: In his priestly state: wearing the priestly garments and fit to serve
For future generations, not only for the first פרה in the desert
And he shall wash his clothes
And he is impure until evening

phrases.english: "And the kohen shall wash his clothes"
in his priestly state.
"And the kohen shall be impure until evening"
a kohen in his priestly state, for future generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the verse-by-verse reading of the פרה passage, moving on to the next verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרה must be done by a כהן בכיהונו, and this applies לדורות.

steps.title: Why say 'in his priestly state' if a High Priest is required?
steps.stepSummary: This rule works well for the view that a כהן הדיוט does the פרה in future generations. But for the view that a כהן גדול is required, why would we need a verse to say he must be בכיהונו?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says that in future generations the פרה is done by an ordinary כהן. But for the one who says it is done by a כהן גדול: once we already need a כהן גדול, do we really need to be told that he must be in his priestly state?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the rule from step 8 against an earlier dispute about who does the פרה לדורות. It challenges whether the word בכיהונו is needed at all according to one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an ordinary כהן does the פרה, it makes sense for the תורה to stress that he must be in full priestly state. But if we already demand a כהן גדול, the highest כהן, it seems obvious that he must also be in proper priestly form. So the verse looks unnecessary for that view.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says…
An ordinary כהן, not the כהן גדול

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
that for future generations it is done by an ordinary kohen: fine,
but according to the one who says
that for future generations it is done by a High Priest,
now that we require a High Priest,
is it necessary to say "in his priestly state"?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the rule in step 8 is needed according to one side of the dispute about פרה לדורות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word בכיהונו according to the view that a כהן גדול does the פרה לדורות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a כהן גדול is required, it is obvious he must be in priestly state, so the verse would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The Torah sometimes writes out something we could have derived ourselves
steps.stepSummary: Yes, it is obvious. But the תורה sometimes writes out something we could have learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Sometimes something could be learned through a קל וחומר, and the verse still takes the trouble to write it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees the rule is obvious for that view. It answers that this is not a problem, because the תורה sometimes spells out what logic would already teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not invent a new reason for the word. Instead it admits it is a קל וחומר and says the verse wrote it anyway. So the extra word does not disprove the view that requires a כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lesser case to a greater one
The verse took the trouble and wrote it

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not finding a hidden new meaning here. It is openly saying the verse repeats what we already knew, and that the תורה sometimes does this.

phrases.english: Yes,
a matter that could be learned through an a fortiori argument
the verse took the trouble and wrote it anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts that the word is extra, and says the תורה sometimes spells out what a קל וחומר would teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An extra word must teach something new, so this view seems to have no use for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה may write out something that could be learned by a קל וחומר, so the extra word causes no difficulty.

steps.title: Who may gather the ashes: a non-kohen and a woman, but not a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor
steps.stepSummary: From "ואסף איש טהור… והניח," the גמרא learns that a זר and an אשה may gather the ashes. A חרש, שוטה and קטן may not, because they lack the understanding to place them.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And a pure man shall gather the ashes of the heifer and place them." "Man" allows a non-כהן. "Pure" allows even a woman. "And place" requires someone with the understanding to place them, which excludes a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor, who lack that understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next stage of the פרה, which is gathering the ashes. It learns from three words in the verse who is allowed to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "איש" rather than "כהן" shows a זר may gather. "טהור" puts the stress on being pure rather than on being a man, so an אשה is also allowed. "והניח" requires understanding of what one is doing, which excludes those הלכה treats as lacking דעת.

keyTerms.meaning: The ashes of the פרה אדומה
A deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor

phrases.english: "And a pure man shall gather
the ashes of the heifer and place them."
"Man" makes a non-kohen eligible,
"pure" makes a woman eligible,
"and place" means someone who has the understanding to place them,
which excludes a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor,
who do not have the understanding to place them.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the stages of the פרה have different eligibility rules. Gathering the ashes is much more open than slaughtering or sprinkling.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָסַף אִישׁ טָהוֹר אֵת אֵפֶר הַפָּרָה וְהִנִּיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next verse and the next stage of the פרה service, gathering the ashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זר and an אשה may gather the ashes. A חרש, שוטה and קטן may not.

steps.title: Quoting a משנה about who may sanctify the water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in מסכת פרה: everyone may do קידוש except a חרש, שוטה and קטן. רבי יהודה allows a קטן but disqualifies an אשה and an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Everyone is eligible to sanctify, except a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor. רבי יהודה allows a minor, but disqualifies a woman and an androgynous person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה about the next stage, קידוש (putting the ashes into the water). This is a setup line that prepares the next move, where the גמרא will read the verse about this stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא's list matches step 11: everyone is allowed except those without דעת. רבי יהודה differs in two ways: he allows a קטן but rules out an אשה and an אנדרוגינוס. The גמרא will soon look for the verse behind this dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere (here, מסכת פרה)
To sanctify: put the ashes into the water
A person with both male and female features

steps.confusionAlert: Here "לקדש" does not mean making קידוש on wine. It means mixing the פרה ashes with water to make the purifying water.

phrases.english: We learned in a mishnah there:
Everyone is eligible to sanctify,
except a deaf-mute, an imbecile and a minor.
Rabbi Yehuda allows a minor,
but disqualifies a woman and an androgynous person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from gathering the ashes to the next stage, קידוש, by quoting a משנה as a setup for reading the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: everyone may do קידוש except a חרש, שוטה and קטן. רבי יהודה: a קטן may, but an אשה and an אנדרוגינוס may not.

steps.title: What is the source for the view of רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the view of רבנן (the תנא קמא) in the משנה about קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the Rabbis?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבנן disqualify a חרש, שוטה and קטן from קידוש. This question sets up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה just quoted, רבנן disqualify only חרש, שוטה and קטן, and they allow an אשה. The גמרא wants to find which verse produces exactly this list.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (here, the first, unnamed opinion in the משנה)
Putting the פרה ashes into the spring water to make מי חטאת

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: This means the תנא קמא, the first opinion in the משנה in פרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source behind the first opinion in the משנה quoted in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that teaches רבנן's list of who is disqualified from קידוש.

steps.title: The plural 'they shall take' links mixing to gathering
steps.stepSummary: The verse uses the plural ״וְלָקְחוּ״, meaning 'they' who did the gathering. So whoever is disqualified from אסיפה is disqualified from קידוש, and whoever is fit for אסיפה is fit for קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they shall take for the impure person from the ashes of the burning of the sin-offering.' Those whom I disqualified for you in gathering, I disqualified for you in mixing. Those whom I made fit for you in gathering, I made fit for you in mixing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״וְלָקְחוּ״ ("they") points back to the same people who gathered the ashes. Whatever rules applied to gathering also apply to mixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 taught that a זר and an אשה may gather the ashes, but a חרש, שוטה and קטן may not. The word "they" carries that same list over to קידוש. This explains why רבנן allow an אשה but disqualify a קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: Gathering the ashes of the פרה

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates one shared list of who may do both stages of the פרה אדומה ashes.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And they shall take for the impure person
from the ashes of the burning of the sin-offering."
Those whom I disqualified for you in gathering
phrases.notes: Spoken as if from the Torah's point of view.

phrases.english: I disqualified for you in mixing;
and those whom I made fit for you in gathering
I made fit for you in mixing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural ״וְלָקְחוּ״ ties קידוש to אסיפה, so the same people are fit or unfit for both.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads the plural as including a minor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that if the verse only wanted to link mixing to gathering, it could have said ״וְלָקַח״ in the singular. The plural comes to add someone: even a קטן, who may not gather, may mix.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? If so, let the verse say 'and he shall take.' Why does it say 'and they shall take'? To teach that even a minor, whom I disqualified for you there, is fit here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה rejects the reading of רבנן. He says the plural word comes to add a קטן to קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the link to gathering does not need a plural, because a singular word would have worked just as well. So the extra plural must teach something new: a קטן is fit for קידוש even though he is unfit for אסיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who allows a קטן to do קידוש

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same word ״וְלָקְחוּ״. רבנן use it to tie mixing to gathering. רבי יהודה uses it to include a קטן beyond the gathering list.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, how does he respond?
If so, let the verse say "and he shall take"!
Why does it say "and they shall take"?
To teach that even a minor, whom I disqualified for you there (in gathering),
here (in mixing) is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אִם כֵּן לֵימָא קְרָא ״וְלָקַח״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the derivation of רבנן from Step 14 and reads the same word differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using ״וְלָקְחוּ״ only to link קידוש to אסיפה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A singular word would have been enough for that link, so the plural must teach an addition: a קטן.

steps.title: Where does רבי יהודה learn that a woman is unfit?
steps.stepSummary: If the plural includes even a קטן, how does רבי יהודה exclude an אשה from קידוש?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does he learn that a woman is unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי יהודה's source for disqualifying an אשה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשה may gather the ashes, and רבי יהודה reads the plural as including people, not excluding them. So his ruling that an אשה is unfit for קידוש needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: A woman, from where does he (Rabbi Yehuda) learn that she is unfit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with רבי יהודה's view and asks for his second ruling from Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that teaches רבי יהודה that an אשה cannot do קידוש.

steps.title: 'He shall put', not 'she shall put'
steps.stepSummary: The verse says ״וְנָתַן״ (masculine) and not ״וְנָתְנָה״ (feminine). This teaches that an אשה may not put the ashes in.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall put', and not 'and she shall put.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the verse uses the masculine form ״וְנָתַן״. This excludes an אשה from the act of putting the ashes into the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, ״וְלָקְחוּ״ adds a קטן, and ״וְנָתַן״ takes away an אשה. This exactly matches his opinion in the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: ״וְלָקְחוּ״ includes a קטן, and ״וְנָתַן״ excludes an אשה. רבנן: ״וְלָקְחוּ״ copies the gathering list, so an אשה is fit and a קטן is unfit.

phrases.english: "And he shall put", and not "and she shall put."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The masculine ״וְנָתַן״ excludes an אשה from קידוש.

steps.title: רבנן: the plural teaches that the taker and the putter may differ
steps.stepSummary: רבנן explain that if both words were singular, we would think one person must both take and put. So the תורה wrote ״וְלָקְחוּ״ in the plural.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis? If the Merciful One had written 'and he shall take… and he shall put,' I would have said it is not valid until one person takes and the same one puts. So the Merciful One wrote 'and they shall take.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבנן deal with the mix of plural and singular in the verse. They say the mix teaches a rule about how many people may do the steps, not about who is excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן do not read ״וְנָתַן״ as excluding an אשה. Instead, they say the plural ״וְלָקְחוּ״ teaches that the taking does not have to be done by the same single person who puts the ashes in.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a mistaken first assumption)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, how do they explain it?
If the Merciful One had written "and he shall take… and he shall put,"
I would have said:
it is not valid until one person takes and that same one puts;
so the Merciful One wrote "and they shall take."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבנן and explains how they use the verse's wording without excluding an אשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse's wording to teach a different rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With two singular words, one person would have to both take and put.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural ״וְלָקְחוּ״ allows the taking to be done by someone other than the person who puts.

steps.title: Two may take and one may put
steps.stepSummary: If both words were plural, we would think two people must take and two must put. So the תורה wrote a plural followed by a singular: two may take and one may put.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Merciful One had written 'and they shall take… and they shall put,' I would have said it is not valid until two take and two put. So the Merciful One wrote 'and they shall take… and he shall put,' to teach that even if two take and one puts, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation of רבנן. It shows why the Torah used one plural and one singular, and not two plurals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two plurals would have required two people for each step. The mix of plural and singular teaches that two people may take while one person puts. So for רבנן, ״וְנָתַן״ is about how many people put the ashes in, not about excluding an אשה.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבנן, the plural-then-singular wording teaches how many people may take and put: two may take and one may put. It does not exclude an אשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how each side accounts for every word of the verse. That is why their practical lists of who may do קידוש come out differently.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written "and they shall take… and they shall put,"
I would have said:
it is not valid until two take and two put;
so the Merciful One wrote "and they shall take… and he shall put,"
to teach that even if two take and one puts, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part explanation of רבנן that began in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the verse's wording to teach a different rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With two plural words, two people would be required for each step.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plural then singular: two may take and one may put, and the rite is valid.

steps.title: רבנן read 'a pure man' for dipping the hyssop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next stage, taking and dipping the hyssop. According to רבנן, ״אִישׁ״ excludes an אשה and ״טָהוֹר״ includes a קטן.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And a pure man shall take hyssop and dip it in the water." According to the Rabbis: "man" means a man and not a woman. "Pure" comes to qualify a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reads the verse about the next stage, dipping the hyssop into the water, and explains how רבנן learn it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of ״אִישׁ טָהוֹר״ teaches something. ״אִישׁ״ (a man) leaves out an אשה. ״טָהוֹר״ is extra, since everyone involved must be pure anyway, so it is used to include a קטן. This is the reverse of רבנן's view on the earlier stage of קידוש, where they qualified an אשה but not a קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: Hyssop, the plant dipped into the water and used to sprinkle
To qualify, to make someone valid for the task

phrases.english: "And he shall take hyssop and dip it in the water
phrases.notes: במדבר יט:יח. This is the stage after the ashes are put into the water.

phrases.english: a pure man"
phrases.notes: The גמרא is about to learn something from these two words.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis: "man" means a man, but not a woman.
"Pure" comes to qualify the minor.
phrases.notes: Even a קטן may dip, as long as he is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָקַח אֵזוֹב וְטָבַל בַּמַּיִם אִישׁ טָהוֹר לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the earlier stage of putting the ashes in, the גמרא moves on to the verse for the next stage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבנן, a קטן may dip the hyssop but an אשה may not.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads the same words the opposite way
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, ״אִישׁ״ excludes a קטן and ״טָהוֹר״ includes an אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה: "man" means an adult and not a minor. "Pure" comes to qualify a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יהודה reads the same two words with the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, ״אִישׁ″ stresses an adult, so it leaves out a קטן. The extra word ״טָהוֹר״ then includes an אשה. So for this stage, רבי יהודה qualifies an אשה but not a קטן, which is the reverse of his view on the earlier stage.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child below the age of מצוות
But not, used to exclude someone

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two views. רבנן: no אשה, yes קטן. רבי יהודה: no קטן, yes אשה. Each one reverses his own view from the previous stage.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda: "man" means an adult, but not a minor.
"Pure" comes to qualify the woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's reading of the same verse that רבנן just explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, an אשה may dip the hyssop but a קטן may not.

steps.title: A משנה rejects a woman for sprinkling but accepts a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: everyone may sprinkle except a טומטום, an אנדרוגינוס, and an אשה, while a קטן with understanding may sprinkle with an אשה helping him. This seems to contradict רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Everyone is qualified to sprinkle, except a טומטום, an אנדרוגינוס, and a woman. And a minor who has understanding: a woman helps him and he sprinkles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view just given for רבי יהודה by quoting a משנה about sprinkling the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an אשה is not allowed to sprinkle, but a קטן is. That matches רבנן exactly. It is the opposite of what we just said in the name of רבי יהודה, who qualifies an אשה and rejects a קטן. So the משנה seems to be a problem for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
A person whose gender cannot be seen
A person with both male and female features
Understanding, enough maturity to know what he is doing

steps.confusionAlert: The אשה only helps, for example by holding the water. The קטן is the one who actually sprinkles. So the משנה still treats the אשה as not qualified to sprinkle.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a direct clash between a משנה and רבי יהודה's reading. The גמרא will now need to resolve it.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Everyone is qualified to sprinkle,
except for a tumtum, an androginus, and a woman.
And a minor who has understanding:
phrases.notes: A קטן is qualified if he understands what he is doing.

phrases.english: a woman helps him, and he sprinkles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the view just stated in the name of רבי יהודה for this stage.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that ״טָהוֹר״ qualifies an אשה and ״אִישׁ״ excludes a קטן for dipping and sprinkling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rejects an אשה and accepts a קטן for sprinkling, which is the exact opposite of רבי יהודה's reading.
